mcqs.question: A convex lens forms a real image of a small object placed 30 cm in front of the lens. The image is formed 60 cm on the opposite side of the lens. What is the magnification of the image?
mcqs.explanation: Using the Cartesian sign convention, object distance u = -30 cm (object on the incident side) and image distance v = +60 cm (real image on the opposite side). Magnification m = v / u = (+60) / (-30) = -2. The negative sign indicates the image is inverted and its size is twice that of the object. Many students mistakenly take magnification as +2, ignoring the sign convention.

mcqs.question: A convex lens has a focal length of 20 cm. What is the power of this lens in dioptres?
mcqs.explanation: Power P of a lens is defined as the reciprocal of its focal length (in metres): P = 1/f. Here f = 20 cm = 0.20 m, so P = 1 / 0.20 = 5 dioptres. The power is positive for a converging (convex) lens. Options B and D use incorrect units, and option C gives a negative sign which applies to diverging lenses.

mcqs.question: Lens A is a converging lens with focal length 15 cm, and Lens B is a diverging lens with focal length -30 cm. Which lens has the greater magnitude of optical power?
mcqs.explanation: Power P = 1/f (in metres). For Lens A: f = 15 cm = 0.15 m, so P_A = 1/0.15 ≈ +6.67 D. For Lens B: f = -30 cm = -0.30 m, so P_B = 1/(-0.30) ≈ -3.33 D. The magnitudes are |6.67| and |3.33| respectively; therefore Lens A has the larger magnitude of power. Option B is incorrect because its magnitude is smaller, and options C and D are clearly false.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand combination of lens powers at the required level
mcqs.question: Two thin lenses are placed in contact: a converging lens of power +4 D and a diverging lens of power -2 D. What is the effective focal length of the combination?
mcqs.explanation: When thin lenses are in contact, their powers add: P_total = +4 D + (‑2 D) = +2 D. The effective focal length f_total = 1 / P_total = 1 / 2 D = 0.5 m (or 50 cm). Option B matches this result. Options A, C, and D correspond to incorrect total powers.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 12 cm in front of a convex lens whose focal length is 4 cm. Using the lens formula (1/f = 1/v + 1/u), what is the image distance v?
mcqs.explanation: Apply the lens formula with sign convention: u = -12 cm (object in front of lens), f = +4 cm. 1/4 = 1/v + 1/(-12) ⇒ 1/v = 1/4 + 1/12 = 3/12 + 1/12 = 4/12 = 1/3 ⇒ v = +3 cm. The positive sign indicates a real image on the opposite side of the lens. Option A is correct; the other options do not satisfy the formula.

mcqs.question: A concave lens forms a virtual image 20 cm on the same side as the object, which is placed 10 cm in front of the lens. According to the Cartesian sign convention, what is the sign of the image distance v?
mcqs.explanation: In the Cartesian sign convention, distances measured in the direction of incident light (from object towards lens) are taken as negative. For a virtual image formed on the same side as the object, the image distance v is measured opposite to the direction of incident light, so v is negative. Hence option B is correct. Positive would apply to real images on the opposite side; zero and undefined are not applicable.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes magnification from the power of a lens?

options.A: Magnification is the ratio of image height to object height, while power is the reciprocal of the focal length.
options.B: Magnification is the reciprocal of the focal length, while power is the ratio of image height to object height.
options.C: Both magnification and power are defined as the ratio of image distance to object distance.
options.D: Magnification and power are unrelated concepts.

mcqs.answer: Magnification is the ratio of image height to object height, while power is the reciprocal of the focal length.
mcqs.explanation: Magnification (m) = image height / object height = v / u (using sign convention). Power (P) = 1 / f (in metres) and indicates the lens's ability to converge or diverge light. Option A accurately describes both definitions. Options B, C, and D mix up the definitions or claim no relation, which is incorrect.

mcqs.question: A thin lens has a focal length of 0.25 m. What is the power of this lens?
mcqs.explanation: Power P = 1 / f (in metres). Here f = 0.25 m, so P = 1 / 0.25 = 4 dioptres. Since the focal length is positive, the lens is converging, giving a positive power. Option A is correct; option B would correspond to a diverging lens, and options C and D are numerically incorrect.
